title: Capability Artefact (v1.1.0)
description: A business capability — what the organisation must be able to do, expressed in business terms, technology-agnostic. Multi-dimensional per TOGAF G189: organisation, people, processes, technology.

demand_assumption.description: Optional. The demand this capability answers, recorded as an explicit assumption where no outcome is linked yet. Satisfies the demand part of definition-ladder rung R1 in place of required_by_outcomes.

open_questions.description: Optional marker. States that the capability has no open question with more than one credible answer, so no consideration is expected to affect it. Satisfies the consideration part of definition-ladder rung R2. Omit it when considerations exist.

flows.description: Optional. Named paths through the capability that someone would recognise as a job being done. Each carries its rung on the definition ladder (standards/capabilities/standard-definition-ladder.md). The capability sits on the rung of its lowest flow. A recorded rung is a claim; a derived rung (aaa-rung) wins where available.

id.description: Kebab-case identifier, unique within the capability.

rung.description: Recorded rung on the definition ladder, R0 to R6.

allOf.$comment: L1 capabilities have no parent; L2/L3 must have one.

else.$comment: L1 — parent should be null or omitted.

allOf.$comment: L3 capabilities are provided by exactly one Platform, so provided_by_platform is required for them; L1/L2 capabilities are cross-platform groupings and may omit it. Realisation by ABBs (realised_by_abbs) is intentionally NOT required, even for L3: an L3 capability with no realising ABB is a legitimate architecture GAP surfaced by gap analysis, not a structural-validity error. The foundation catalogue ships such unrealised placeholders deliberately.
